New Senior Lender: means a financial institution or other entity that becomes a party to the Senior Facility Agreement by way of an assignment or transfer from an existing Senior Lender, thereby assuming the rights and obligations of the original lender.
“Northern Irish Borrower” means any Borrower that, at the time that they enter into a Borrower Agreement, is resident in Northern Ireland.

“Northern Irish Receivable Recharacterisation Event” means any judgment, decree, declaration, decision or order (whether interim or final) of any supervisory authority, tribunal, court or other governmental authority that requires any Receivable originated by the Seller or other unsecured personal loan (whether originated by [PARTY_NAME] or any other party) entered into with a borrower or consumer resident in Northern Ireland, to be subject to, or otherwise construed in accordance with, Northern Irish law (in whole or in part) in accordance with overriding mandatory provisions of Northern Irish law, rather than the law which the Receivable or unsecured personal loan is expressed to be governed in accordance with its contractual terms.
“Northern Irish Receivables” means Receivables which derive from Borrower Agreements that are governed by, subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Northern Irish law.

Notice of Collections Account Declaration of Trust: A formal legal notice sent by the Seller (originator) to the bank holding the collections account. This notice informs the bank that the funds deposited into the account, which represent collections from the securitized assets, are held in trust for the benefit of the securitization SPV or trustee. Its purpose is to perfect the security interest over the account and ensure the bank acknowledges the trust structure, preventing the commingling of funds and protecting them in the event of the Seller's insolvency.
“Notice of Security” means a notice of security in form and substance satisfactory to the Facility Agent and the Security Trustee.

Offer: means a formal proposal made by the Seller (Originator) to the Purchaser (SPV) under a Receivables Purchase Agreement to sell a specific portfolio of receivables. This proposal typically includes details of the receivables being sold, the proposed purchase price, and relevant representations and warranties regarding their eligibility.

Offer Date: means the specific date on which the Seller formally offers to sell a portfolio of eligible receivables to the Purchaser under the terms of the Receivables Purchase Agreement. This offer typically triggers the purchase process for a given collection period.

“Official Body” means any government, national or supranational body or political subdivision of any of them or any agency, authority, bureau, central bank, commission or department of any government or political subdivision, or any court, tribunal, grand jury or arbitrator, or any agency, authority, regulatory body, court, central bank, stock exchange or other entity exercising executive, legislative, judicial, tax, regulatory or administrative powers or functions of or pertaining to government, or any accounting board or authority (whether or not a part of government) which is responsible for the establishment or interpretation of national or international accounting principles.

Optional Repayment Notice: means a formal written notification provided by the borrower (Issuer) to the lender under a Senior Facility Agreement, stating its intention to voluntarily repay all or part of the senior loan before its scheduled maturity date. This notice typically specifies the proposed repayment amount and date, and is a prerequisite for making an optional prepayment.
“Original Mezzanine Funding Agent” means each persons who is a Mezzanine Funding Agent on the Closing Date.
“Original Mezzanine Note Purchaser” means each person who is a Mezzanine Note Purchaser on the Closing Date.

Original Programme Scheduled Termination Date: means the initial date specified in the Master Framework Agreement on which the securitization programme is scheduled to conclude. This date typically marks when all outstanding securities are expected to be fully repaid and is distinguished from any subsequent dates that may result from an extension of the programme's term.

“Original Senior Lender Group” means the Original Senior Lender and any of its Affiliates, Related Funds and any conduit purchaser entity that it administers or is administered by an Affiliate or Related Fund of the Original Senior Lender.
“Origination Date” means the date on which a Receivable is originated.
“Outstanding Principal Balance” means, in respect of any Receivable, as at any date of determination, the unpaid principal amounts due in respect of it from the relevant Borrower as at that date.
“Paying Transaction Party” means, where any party is under an obligation created by a Transaction Document to make a payment to a Receiving Transaction Party, the party who is to make such payment.

“Permanent Establishment” means:

a fixed place of business (including, without prejudice to the generality of that expression, a place of management, branch, office, factory, workshop, installation or structure used for the exploration of natural resources, mine, oil or gas well, quarry or any other place of extraction of natural resources, building site or construction or installation project) through or in which the business of the Issuer is wholly or partly carried on; or

an agent or other person acting on behalf of the Issuer that has, and habitually exercises, authority to do business on behalf of the Issuer other than an agent of independent status acting in the ordinary course of his business.

“Permitted Transferee” means any Affiliate of the Senior Lender provided that, following such transfer or assignment, the Issuer will not be required by law to make any withholding or deduction from any amounts payable to the transferee or assignee in respect of the Senior Facility or otherwise to pay increased costs in accordance with the increased costs indemnity.

Personal Data: means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. This includes, but is not limited to, names, identification numbers, location data, online identifiers (like IP addresses), and any information specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that person. In a securitization context, this often pertains to information about the underlying obligors of the assets being securitized.

Portfolio Trustee: means the entity, typically a professional trust company, appointed under a securitization agreement (such as a Receivables Purchase Agreement) to hold the portfolio of purchased receivables and related assets on trust. The Portfolio Trustee holds the legal title to these assets for the benefit of the beneficiaries of the trust (e.g., the noteholders or the security trustee), ensuring asset segregation and bankruptcy remoteness from the originator.

Post-Enforcement Priority of Payments: refers to the specific sequence in which funds are distributed after an enforcement event (such as a default) has been triggered. This payment waterfall dictates the order of payments to various parties, including trustees, servicers, hedge counterparties, and different tranches of noteholders, from the proceeds of the liquidated collateral. It typically prioritizes senior secured creditors over junior and unsecured creditors.

“Potential Early Amortisation Event” means an event that would, with the giving of notice, lapse of time, making of any determination or any combination thereof, constitute an Early Amortisation Event.
“Potential Insolvency Proceedings” means an event that would, with the giving of notice, lapse of time, making of any determination or any combination thereof, constitute Insolvency Proceedings.

“Potential Investor” means any potential transferee of a Senior Commitment or Mezzanine Note that has complied with the requirements of Clause 24 (Confidentiality) of the Master Framework Agreement and would satisfy any transfer restrictions in the Transaction Documents.

“Potential Mezzanine Event of Default” means an event that would, with the giving of notice, lapse of time, making of any determination or any combination thereof, constitute a Mezzanine Event of Default.

“Potential Servicer Termination Event” means an event that would, with the giving of notice, lapse of time, making of any determination or any combination thereof, constitute a Servicer Termination Event.

Pre-Enforcement Priority of Payments: refers to the contractual order, often called a 'payment waterfall', that dictates how cash flows generated by the securitized assets are distributed among various parties before an enforcement event (such as a default) occurs. This priority typically ensures that senior expenses (e.g., trustee and servicer fees) and interest payments to the most senior noteholders are paid first, followed by payments to more junior tranches, with any remaining funds flowing to the equity holders or originator. This structure is fundamental to creating the different risk-return profiles of the securitization's tranches.

“Pre-Funding Account” means any pre-funding account in the name of the Issuer designated in writing by the Seller, Issuer and the Facility Agent, from time to time, to fall within this definition and maintained at all times at an Account Bank Eligible Institution.
“Pre-Funding Account Mezzanine Ledger” means the ledger in the Pre-Funding Account to which the Mezzanine Pre-Funding Account Amount is credited.
“Pre-Funding Limit” means the amount that is equal to the aggregate of the Senior Pre-Funding Limit and the Mezzanine Pre-Funding Limit.

The amount returned to holders of Mezzanine Notes when funds from a pre-funding account are not fully used to purchase collateral assets within the specified pre-funding period. This repayment effectively constitutes a partial redemption of the mezzanine notes, reducing the issuer's outstanding debt to match the final size of the collateral pool.

Pre-Funding Senior Repayment Amount: means the mandatory repayment of the senior loan by the Issuer using funds from a Pre-Funding Account. This repayment is typically triggered when the funds are not used to purchase eligible assets within a specified pre-funding period, thereby reducing the lender's exposure and the issuer's interest costs on unused capital.

“Prime Borrower” means a Borrower that, where used for the purposes of underwriting and responsible lending assessment, has obtained:

a Gauge 2 Score of at least 591; and

a Delphi 11SBN Score of at least 791.

Principal Amount Outstanding: means, as of any given date, the total remaining unpaid principal portion of a loan, note, or other debt instrument. It is calculated as the original principal amount of the debt, reduced by any principal repayments made to date, and does not include any accrued but unpaid interest. In a multi-tranche facility, it is often calculated separately for each tranche (e.g., senior, mezzanine) and then aggregated to determine the total outstanding principal for the entire facility.

Principles of Construction: refers to the set of rules and guidelines specified in an agreement for its interpretation. These principles ensure clarity and consistency and typically cover aspects such as the treatment of singular and plural nouns, gendered pronouns, headings, references to statutes, and the meaning of terms like 'including'. They provide a framework for resolving any ambiguities in the contract's language.

Priority of Payments: Refers to the contractual order in which cash flows generated by the securitized assets are distributed among various parties involved in the transaction. This is often called the 'waterfall'. It distinguishes between a 'Pre-Enforcement Priority of Payments' for normal operating conditions and a 'Post-Enforcement Priority of Payments' which applies after a default or other trigger event, typically redirecting funds to repay senior noteholders more quickly.

Privacy Commitments: means the representations, warranties, and covenants made by the Seller and/or Servicer in a securitization agreement. These commitments confirm their adherence to all applicable data protection laws (such as GDPR or CCPA) regarding the collection, use, storage, processing, and security of personal data associated with the obligors and the underlying securitized assets.

“Profit” means, in respect of any person or group, the profit before tax for the most recent financial period as shown in its most recent financial accounts (being its monthly management accounts for each relevant period).

“Pro Rata Share” means:

for any Senior Lender:

the Senior Commitment of such Senior Lender, divided by the Senior Total Commitments; and

after the Senior Total Commitments have been reduced to zero, the Senior Principal Amounts Outstanding funded by such Senior Lender, divided by the aggregate Senior Principal Amount Outstanding of the Senior Loans funded by all Senior Lenders; and

for any Mezzanine Note Purchaser:

the Mezzanine Commitment of such Mezzanine Note Purchaser, divided by the Mezzanine Total Commitments; and

after the Mezzanine Total Commitments have been reduced to zero, the Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the Mezzanine Notes funded by such Mezzanine Note Purchaser, divided by the Mezzanine Principal Amount Outstanding of the Mezzanine Notes funded by all Mezzanine Note Purchasers.

“Programme Scheduled Termination Date” means the later of:

if, at any time prior to the date falling one year after the Closing Date, the Original Senior Lender delivers notice in writing to the Seller that the “Programme Scheduled Termination Date” is the Monthly Payment Date occurring on or immediately after the date falling 24 months after the Closing Date, the Monthly Payment Date occurring on or immediately after the date falling 24 months after the Closing Date;

if no notice is delivered in accordance with paragraph (a) above, the Monthly Payment Date occurring on or immediately after the date falling 36 months after the Closing Date; or

any other Monthly Payment Date agreed between the parties in writing, from time to time, in accordance with Clause 3.5 (Extension of the Programme Scheduled Termination Date) of the Master Framework Agreement.

“Purchase Date” means, in respect of any Receivable, any calendar day occurring in the Revolving Period on which the relevant Seller wishes to sell the Receivable to the Issuer in accordance with the terms of the Receivables Purchase Agreement, or as the context requires, the Business Day on which the Issuer has purchased the Receivable from the relevant Seller.

“Purchase Date Condition” means, in respect of any Business Day during the Revolving Period that the Servicer wishes to deem a Purchase Date, the condition that must be satisfied on that date, being that a duly completed List of Receivables has been delivered by the relevant Seller to the Issuer and the Facility Agent on that date, recording the Receivables in respect of which Initial Purchase Price has been paid on that Purchase Date that is also a Subordinated Settlement Date (or otherwise payment of Initial Purchase Price is to be paid by way of Subordinated Advances made in accordance with the Subordinated Facilities Agreement).

Purchase Notice: means a formal, written notification delivered by an option holder to a seller to exercise a contractual right to purchase assets. In the context of a Master Framework Agreement, this notice formally triggers the 'Option to Purchase the Senior Loans', specifying the loans to be bought, the purchase price, and the settlement details.
“PurchasePrice” means, in respect of each Receivable, its Initial Purchase Price.

PurchasePrice Payment Obligation: Means the contractual obligation of a buyer to pay the agreed purchase price for an asset or portfolio of assets (such as receivables in a securitization) as defined in a master agreement. This obligation is often structured to be settled not only through direct payment but also potentially through set-off arrangements involving a subordinated loan facility, where funds from the facility are used to satisfy all or part of the purchase price.

“Purchased Receivable” means, as at any date of determination, any Receivable which has been purchased (or purported to have been purchased) by the Issuer that remains outstanding at that time and which has not been repurchased or re-transferred by the Seller in accordance with the terms of the Transaction Documents.

“Push Payment” means any payment that is:

made manually by a Borrower; or

made by a third party (other than an Employer Partner) in the context of an IVA or a debt management plan.

Push Payments Concentration Percentage: means a threshold, expressed as a percentage, that limits the maximum allowable portion of a securitized asset pool consisting of receivables settled through 'push payment' methods (where the debtor initiates the payment, e.g., wire transfer). This concentration limit is designed to mitigate risks associated with specific payment types, such as operational delays, fraud, or inconsistent cash flow, thereby ensuring the overall quality and diversification of the collateral pool.

Push Payments Excess Concentration Amount: means the monetary value of receivables generated from 'Push Payments' (transactions initiated by the payer) that exceeds the maximum permitted concentration limit for this specific type of receivable, as defined in the transaction documents. This mechanism is a risk management tool in securitization designed to prevent over-reliance on a single payment method. If this amount is positive, the excess receivables are typically excluded from the eligible asset pool or trigger other contractual consequences.

QFC (Qualified Financial Contract): means a broad category of financial agreements including securities contracts, commodity contracts, forward contracts, repurchase agreements, and swap agreements, as defined under U.S. law (12 U.S.C. § 5390(c)(8)(D)). These contracts receive special treatment during the resolution of a failing financial institution, allowing regulators to stay counterparty termination rights and transfer the contracts to a stable entity to prevent widespread financial disruption.

QFC Credit Support: means any collateral, margin, guarantee, or other form of credit enhancement that supports a party's obligations under a Qualified Financial Contract (QFC). This support is subject to specific treatment under U.S. financial regulations (like the QFC Stay Rules), which temporarily restrict a counterparty's ability to seize or liquidate this support if a systemically important financial institution enters a resolution or insolvency proceeding.

“Qualifying Bank” means a person or entity which effectively conducts banking activities with its own infrastructure and staff as its principal purpose and which has a banking license in full force and effect issued in accordance with the banking laws in force in its jurisdiction of incorporation, or if acting through a branch, issued in accordance with the banking laws in the jurisdiction of such branch, all in accordance with the guidelines.
“RAO” means The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Regulated Activities) Order 2001 (as amended from time to time).

“Receivable” means all amounts owing by a Borrower, present and future, absolute or contingent, due now or in the future (including, without limitation, any Finance Charges), from time to time, arising under a Borrower Agreement in respect of a Consumer Loan to a Borrower in the United Kingdom.
“Receivables Purchase Agreement” means the receivables purchase agreement, dated on or about the Signing Date between the Issuer, the Security Trustee, the Sellers and the Facility Agent.

Receivables Warranties: A series of contractual representations and guarantees made by the Seller of receivables to the Purchaser (typically an SPV or Issuer) at the time of sale. These warranties confirm the quality, validity, and key characteristics of the receivables, such as their legal enforceability, the accuracy of their stated balances, their compliance with underwriting standards, and their freedom from liens or disputes. A breach of these warranties typically obligates the Seller to repurchase or substitute the non-compliant receivable, thereby protecting the securitization vehicle from credit losses arising from defective assets.

Receiver: An insolvency practitioner or other qualified individual appointed by the Security Trustee under the terms of the Security Agreement, typically following an Event of Default. The Receiver's primary role is to take control of the charged assets, manage them, and ultimately realize their value (through sale or other means) in order to repay the secured creditors.

Recipient: means the party receiving a supply of goods or services who, under a reverse charge mechanism, is liable to account for and pay the Value Added Tax (VAT) on that supply directly to the relevant tax authority, rather than the supplier.

Recognised Stock Exchange: means a stock exchange that is officially designated as such by the relevant tax authority (e.g., HMRC in the UK under the Income Tax Act). This designation typically includes major national exchanges (like the London Stock Exchange) and certain regulated alternative trading venues (like multilateral trading facilities). The status is crucial for determining the tax treatment of securities and investments and for meeting regulatory requirements for qualifying holdings.

Recovered Amount: means any sum received or recovered by a creditor (in this context, the Senior Lender) from an obligor or through the enforcement of security following a default. Under a sharing clause, if this amount exceeds the lender's proportional entitlement from the shared collateral pool, the excess portion must be paid to other creditors to ensure an equitable distribution of proceeds as per the agreed waterfall.

Recovering Funding Party: means a lender in a syndicated financing arrangement who receives a payment (a 'Sharing Payment') that is disproportionately large compared to its pro-rata share of the debt. The agreement obligates this party to share the excess portion of the payment with the other lenders in the syndicate to ensure all receive an equitable distribution of recovered funds.

Redistributed Amount: means the specific amount of funds previously allocated or paid to a party in the transaction waterfall that must be returned or clawed back following a correction, recalculation, or the occurrence of a trigger event as specified in the 'Reversal of Redistribution' clause. This amount is then re-allocated according to the corrected priority of payments.

“Reduced Rate of Return” means the amount (if any) by which:

exceeds:

the interest which a Senior Lender or a Mezzanine Note Purchaser should have received for the period from the date of receipt of all or any part of its Senior Commitments, Mezzanine Commitments or Unpaid Sum (as applicable) to the last day of the current Interest Period in respect of that Senior Commitment, Mezzanine Commitment or Unpaid Sum, had the principal amount or Unpaid Sum received been paid on the last day of that Interest Period;

the amount which that Senior Lender or that Mezzanine Note Purchaser would be able to obtain by placing an amount equal to the principal amount or Unpaid Sum received by it on deposit with a leading bank in the Relevant Interbank Market for a period starting on the Business Day following receipt or recovery and ending on the last day of the current Interest Period.

Register: means the official record, maintained by the Registrar or a similar agent, which lists the names, addresses, and holdings of the registered owners (Noteholders) of the securities. This register provides the definitive evidence of legal title to the notes, determining who is entitled to receive payments of principal and interest and to exercise other rights associated with the notes.
“Regulators” means the FCA, the Information Commissioner’s Office and the Financial Ombudsman Service.

“Regulatory Requirement” means:

the adoption after the Closing Date of any applicable law, rule or regulation (including any applicable law, rule or regulation regarding capital adequacy or liquidity coverage) or any other change to any law, rule or regulation after the Closing Date;

any change after the Closing Date in the interpretation or administration of any applicable law, rule or regulation by any Official Body charged with the interpretation or administration thereof, or compliance with any request or directive (whether or not having the force of law) of any such Official Body; or

any request, rule, guideline, directive or promulgated by any Official Body (including, any rule, guideline or directive promulgated by the Bank of International Settlements, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (or any successor or similar authority), the United States, any foreign government or any regulatory authority) relating to Basel II or Basel III, whether or not having the force of law, and regardless of the date enacted, adopted, issued or implemented.

Rejected Mezzanine Total Commitments Increase Counter Offer: Means the formal notice or action by which the borrower declines a counter-proposal from the mezzanine lenders regarding a requested increase in the total funding commitment. This situation arises when the borrower requests to increase the mezzanine facility size, the lenders respond with a counter-offer on different terms (e.g., amount, pricing, or conditions), and the borrower subsequently rejects those new terms.

Rejected Senior Total Commitments Increase Counter Offer: means the borrower's formal refusal of a counter-proposal made by senior lenders in response to a request to increase the total loan commitment. This occurs when the borrower does not agree to the new terms (such as revised pricing, fees, or a different increase amount) offered by the lenders for the facility upsize.

Rejecting Party: refers to a key stakeholder in a securitization programme (such as a liquidity provider, credit enhancement provider, or a specific class of noteholders) that formally objects to or votes against a proposal to extend the programme's scheduled termination date. The objection by a Rejecting Party can prevent the extension and typically triggers pre-defined wind-down or amortization procedures for the transaction.

“Related Fund” means, in relation to any person, a fund which is managed or advised by the same investment manager or investment adviser as that person or, if it is managed by a different investment manager or investment adviser, a fund whose investment manager or investment adviser is an Affiliate of such person or of the investment manager or investment adviser of that person.
“Relevant Interbank Market” means the London interbank market.

Relevant Mezzanine Obligations: refers to the specific duties and liabilities of the borrower under a Mezzanine Facility Agreement that are the subject of an assignment. These obligations typically include the repayment of principal, payment of interest (including any PIK interest), and compliance with financial and operational covenants, which are being transferred from the original lender to a new party (the assignee) as specified in the related Assignment Agreement.

Relevant Notice: means a formal written communication, as specified in the transaction documents, issued by a party (typically the Security Trustee or Facility Agent) to another party (such as the servicer, an account bank, or the originator) upon the occurrence of a specified event (e.g., a default or enforcement event). The issuance of such a notice typically triggers specific contractual obligations, such as the redirection of collections or the commencement of enforcement actions against the secured assets.

"Relevant Obligations": means the specific contractual duties, payment liabilities, and covenants of the borrower and other obligors under a Senior Facility Agreement that are being assigned from an existing lender to a new lender. These typically include the obligation to repay principal and interest, comply with financial covenants, and adhere to other terms of the loan.

Relevant Transaction Documents: means the set of core legal agreements that collectively govern a securitization or structured finance transaction. This typically includes the Master Framework Agreement itself, the securitization or pooling and servicing agreement, trust deed, security agreements, servicing agreements, swap agreements, and any other ancillary documents essential to establishing the rights and obligations of the parties. These are the specific documents under which the parties agree to submit to a particular jurisdiction for dispute resolution.

Replacement Benchmark Rate: means an alternative or successor benchmark interest rate (e.g., SOFR, SONIA, €STR) that replaces an original benchmark (like LIBOR) following a trigger event, such as the original rate's cessation or declaration as non-representative. The mechanism for determining the replacement rate, often a "waterfall" of options, and any applicable spread adjustment to maintain economic equivalence, is typically detailed in the referenced document.

Reporting Entity: means the party, as specified in the Cash Management Agreement, responsible for preparing and distributing periodic reports (such as the Monthly Investor Report) to investors, rating agencies, and other transaction parties. This entity compiles critical data on the performance of the underlying assets, cash collections, and the application of the payment waterfall, ensuring transparency for all stakeholders. The role is often fulfilled by the Servicer or the Cash Manager.

Reporting FI: means a Financial Institution that is required under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) to report information about financial accounts held by U.S. taxpayers to the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or a relevant local tax authority. In the context of a securitization, this could include the Issuer, the Trustee, or other transaction parties who are classified as financial institutions and have such reporting obligations.

Reporting Requirements: means the obligations mandated by securitisation regulations (e.g., Article 7 of the EU/UK Securitisation Regulation) for the originator, sponsor, and SSPE to provide regular and detailed information to investors, competent authorities, and potential investors. This information typically includes quarterly investor reports, detailed data on the underlying exposures (loan-level data), transaction documentation, and performance metrics, all intended to ensure transparency and allow for proper due diligence and monitoring of the securitisation.

“RepurchasePrice” means:

in respect of any Purchased Receivable that is a Defaulted Receivable and is repurchased by the Seller for the purpose of on-selling such Purchased Receivable to any party that is not party to this Transaction or an Affiliate of a party to this Transaction, the purchase price paid by such third party to purchase the Receivable from the Seller; or

in respect of any Purchased Receivable that does not fall within the description set out in limb (a) above, as at the date of its repurchase, an amount equal to its Outstanding Principal Balance, plus any accrued and unpaid interest and fees as at that date and any costs and expenses incurred by the Issuer as a result of the repurchase of that Purchased Receivable.
“Resolution Authority” means any body which has authority to exercise any Write-down and Conversion Powers.
“ResponsibleOfficer” means with respect to any Person, any member of the board of directors, the chief executive officer, the chief financial officer, or the treasurer of such Person.

Retained Interest: means the economic interest a securitization sponsor is required to hold in a transaction to comply with U.S. risk retention regulations (e.g., Section 941 of the Dodd-Frank Act). This interest, typically representing at least 5% of the credit risk of the securitized assets, ensures the sponsor has 'skin in the game.' It is commonly held as an eligible horizontal residual interest (the most subordinate tranche), an eligible vertical interest (a pro-rata slice of each security class), or a combination of both.

Revocation Notice: A formal legal notice issued to terminate a Declaration of Trust over a Collections Account in a securitization. This notice cancels the arrangement where an originator holds funds in the account on trust for the SPV, typically following events like the deal's termination, a clean-up call, or full repayment of obligations. Its issuance reverts control of the account's assets as specified in the transaction documents.
“Revolving Period” means the period from (and including) the Closing Date to (but excluding) the Termination Date.
“Risk Retention Rules” means the EU Securitisation Regulation or the UK Securitisation Regulation, as the context requires.
“S&P” means Standard and Poor’s Ratings Group, a division of The McGraw Hill Companies, Inc. or the successor to its rating business.
“Salary” means all amounts owing by an Employer through payroll to an Employee.

“Salary Deduction” means the deductions made from, or adjustments made to, the salary of an Employee for the purpose of the repayment of the Consumer Loan advanced by the Seller to that Employee in accordance with the relevant instruction file.

“Sanctioned Country” means, at any time, a country, region or territory which is itself the subject or target of any Sanctions, including, without limitation, the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic, the so-called Luhansk People’s Republic, the Crimea, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson Regions of Ukraine, Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Syria.

“Sanctions” means all economic or financial sanctions or trade embargoes imposed, administered or enforced from time to time by:

the U.S. government, including those administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the U.S. Department of the Treasury or the U.S. Department of State;

the United Nations Security Council, the European Union, any EU member state and/or the United Kingdom (including those administered by Her Majesty’s Treasury); and/or

any other State in which the Facility Agent, the Senior Lender, any member of the Seller Group, [PARTY_NAME], the Servicer or the Issuer or, in each case, any of its subsidiaries operate.

“Scottish Assignation in Security” means each assignation in security governed by Scots law made between the Issuer, the Security Trustee and the Seller and granted pursuant to clause 4.5 (Scottish Receivables) of the Security Agreement and substantially in the form set out in schedule 2 (Form of Scottish Assignation in Security) to the Security Agreement.
“Scottish Borrower” means any Borrower that, at the time that they enter into a Borrower Agreement, is resident in Scotland.

Scottish Declaration of Trust: A legal instrument used under Scots law in securitization transactions to transfer the beneficial interest in assets (such as receivables) from a seller to an issuer (SPV). Unlike an equitable assignment under English law, this declaration establishes a trust where the seller holds the legal title to the Scottish assets on behalf of the issuer, who becomes the beneficiary. This is a common method for perfecting the issuer's interest in Scottish receivables within a larger UK asset portfolio.

“Scottish Receivable Recharacterisation Event” means:

any judgment, decree, declaration, decision or order (whether interim or final) of any supervisory authority, tribunal, court or other governmental authority that requires any Receivable originated by the Seller or other unsecured personal loan (whether originated by [PARTY_NAME] or any other party) entered into with a borrower or consumer resident in Scotland, to be subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Scots law (in whole or in part) in accordance with overriding mandatory provisions of Scots law or any other relevant provisions of Scots law, rather than the law which the Receivable or unsecured personal loan is expressed to be governed in accordance with its contractual terms; or

a determination by the Facility Agent (acting on the instructions of the Most Senior Lenders (acting reasonably)), that any Purchased Receivable which has been entered into with a borrower or consumer resident in Scotland should be treated as being subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Scots law (in whole or in part), rather than the law which the Purchased Receivable is expressed to be governed by in accordance with its contractual terms, on the basis that such determination is necessary for the protection of the interests of the Issuer or any of the Secured Creditors in the Purchased Receivables.
“Scottish Receivables” means Receivables which derive from Borrower Agreements that are governed by, subject to, or otherwise construed as being subject to, Scots law.

“Scottish Trust” means the Scots law trust created pursuant to a Scottish Declaration of Trust in respect of Scottish Receivables which are Purchased Receivables granted pursuant to the procedures referred to in the Receivables Purchase Agreement.

Scottish Trust Property: means the pool of assets (e.g., mortgage receivables, auto loans) governed by Scots law that are held within a Scottish trust for the benefit of security holders in a securitization. This legal structure, distinct from an English trust, is used to ring-fence the assets from the originator's insolvency risk. The specific assets constituting the property for a given transaction are explicitly defined and listed in the applicable Scottish Declaration of Trust document.

Screen Rate: means the benchmark interest rate (such as SOFR, EURIBOR, or SONIA) published on a designated electronic screen service (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg) at a specific time, which is used as the basis for calculating the interest payable on a floating-rate financial instrument, such as a senior loan or note.

Second Currency: refers to the currency in which a payment is actually made or a judgment is obtained, when it differs from the primary currency of the obligation (the 'first currency'). A currency indemnity clause typically requires the obligor to compensate the recipient for any shortfall that arises when converting the second currency back to the first currency due to exchange rate fluctuations.

Financial Asset: means an asset, as defined under UK tax law (Regulation 9A of the Taxation of Securitisation Companies Regulations 2006), that a securitisation company can hold to qualify for a specific tax regime. Master Framework Agreement: means the Master Framework Agreement between, among others, the Issuer, the Seller and the Facility Agent dated as specified in the relevant document (as amended, supplemented or novated from time to time).

Incorporation by Reference Clause: means a clause that imports all definitions from a primary governing document (the Master Framework Agreement) into a supplementary document (a deed of accession), ensuring terminological consistency across the transaction's legal framework without repeating lengthy definition sections, which is crucial in complex multi-document structures like securitizations.

Relevant Notice: means a notice that its rights as chargee, assignee or beneficiary under the relevant charge, absolute assignment by way of security or guarantee described in clauses 4 (Security) and 5 (Floating Charge) of the Security Agreement, have become exercisable.
Information: means any analysis, model, compilation, study, report or other document produced in connection with the Transaction Documents.
Erroneous Payment: means a payment of an amount by the Facility Agent to another Transaction Party which the Facility Agent determines (in its sole discretion) was made in error.

Incorporation by Reference Principle: means the principle that terms defined in, or incorporated by reference into, the Master Framework Agreement shall have the same meanings in any deed of accession or other supplementary document.
